notes.title: Basket/Chains Physics
notes.notes:
Bad news guys... No more freebies! 

Previously, hitting any part of the chains at any speed would basically drop the disc right in the basket. This is no longer the case... Colliding with the chains will now take into account the disc velocity vector, the vector between the disc position and the basket, and figure out the angle between the two. A greater angle will mean less damping. In other words, the less accurate the putt, the less impact the chains will have. 

I think it's a pretty solid improvement, but feel free to voice your disc content over in over in the [url=https://discord.gg/sDNJdpX5XU]disc golf disc cord[/url]

notes.title: Reverting Lighting Setup
notes.notes:
After a lot of pain and frustration, I've decided to bag it with the baked lighting. I'll spare you the details but after endless failed experimenting, I could not arrive at a good looking AND performative baked lighting solution. SO! I'm reverting to real time lighting... 

A painful experience, but ultimately, it's good news. As light baking takes a lot of time and effort, it will lighten the load/speed up development for future courses if I don't have to bother with it. Happy discing!

notes.title: Some Major Under the Hood Changes
notes.notes:
[b]Hello everyone![/b]

I hope you're enjoying your Memorial Day weekend. Many thanks to our servicemen and women!

I've spent much of the past 48 hours rolling my face back and forth across the keyboard. Despite these repeated episodes of resignation, I managed to update the Disc Golf project to Unity 6 and transition from the soon-to-be-retired Built-in Render Pipeline to the Universal Render Pipeline.

While the benefits of these changes might not be immediately obvious, they lay the groundwork for lots of good things to come.

One side effect of changing pipelines is that many of my custom shaders broke — including the one I used for water. I tried following some tutorials to build new ones, but as a Shader Graph rookie, it might as well have been black magic. Fortunately, I found a pretty solid water asset that I think looks pretty spiffy.

Let me know what you think!


TL;DR
- Updated to Unity 6
- Changed render pipeline from Built-In to URP

notes.title: Disc Golf Playtest Now Open
notes.notes: Hello and welcome to the Disc Golf Playtest! Disc Golf can played by 1 to 4 players locally and aims to simulate both the rules and physics of the real world game. Though it has taken a lot of work to get to this point, it is still very early days and virtually all of the game's design, elements, and mechanics are in the prototype phase. The idea of making this playtest available at this early stage is to allow players to follow along on the development journey as the project evolves from concept to completion! So grab your controller and give it a go! Social media links are coming but for now just have fun :)
